business_problem: The BA needed a privacy-compliant way to reduce the manual effort of turning Requests for Change and user stories into high-quality Jira tickets under increasing workload and limited staff capacity.
solution_summary: The German Federal Employment Agency worked with Capgemini to automate RFC and user-story conversion into Jira tickets using a coordinated on-premises multi-agent architecture. Incoming change requests are first analyzed by a reader agent, then broken into steps by a planner agent, transformed into structured Jira content by a creator agent, and checked for consistency and duplicates by a reviewer agent before human approval. The deployment was built to manage large RFC documents and LLM token limits while fitting the agency’s privacy and security requirements. After pilot integration with selected departments, the system was fully connected to the agency’s local Jira environment and orchestrated with CrewAI using privacy-compliant models including Aleph Alpha, LLaMA, and Mistral. This lets the BA keep all data on premises while automating repetitive formatting, summarization, and copy-paste work so staff can focus on oversight and decision-making.

solution_components.name: reader agent
solution_components.role: Analyzes Requests for Change and user stories to extract the information needed for ticket creation.

solution_components.name: planner agent
solution_components.role: Breaks the extracted request into actionable steps for ticket generation.

solution_components.name: creator agent
solution_components.role: Generates the Jira ticket title, description, category, and metadata.

solution_components.name: reviewer agent
solution_components.role: Checks generated tickets for consistency and duplicates before human approval.

solution_components.name: Jira
solution_components.role: Serves as the agency’s local ticketing environment where the generated work items are created and managed.

solution_components.name: CrewAI
solution_components.role: Coordinates the specialized AI agents inside the agency’s on-premises architecture.

data_flow: RFCs and user stories are read and extracted by the reader agent, decomposed by the planner agent, turned into structured Jira tickets by the creator agent, checked by the reviewer agent, and then sent to human reviewers before entering the agency’s local Jira instance.
business_outcome: The BA automated most ticket creation work, reduced manual effort on summarizing and formatting, and established a reusable on-premises AI agent pattern that fits public-sector privacy and security requirements.
